doc.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Sideman years: J.J., Tyree Glenn, Sweets
title: Touring with Harry 'Sweets' Edison
summary: Sweets used him as a sub, and the quartet toured the eastern and midwestern circuit for a year or more until 1959.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: So after Tyree Glenn, then Henry Sweets Edison seems significant.

Oh yeah, Henry would come in and sub for Tyree and that’s how I got to know him. We got this job—that’s how he knew about me. When he was out on the road he’d always call. If I was available I got the job, if not he got someone else. That was 1957 with J.J. then we toured and went to Sweden from Kiruna to Gothenburg
Yeah we got that part. So who was in the Harry Sweets Edison band with you?
Tommy Potter initially, Jimmy Forrest, Tommy Flanagan and myself.
And where were your performing with Sweets?
We were on the road most of the time. We played Birdland a couple of time but we were mostly out of town
Did you go west or did you stay mostly on the eastern seaboard? Did you go all across the country with Sweets?

We didn’t go to the west coast at all we went as far in as Cleveland probably and as far south as Kansas City, and St. Louis. Cause they had clubs that everybody was familiar with. It was part of a circuit basically.
How long did you work with Sweets and how was it touring with him? Did he live up to his nickname “Sweets”? (Laughs)
Sweets has so many lady friends, he was such a handsome man. He had all these girls all over him all the time, that’s why they called him Sweets.
How was he to work for? How was he as a bandleader?

Oh he was phenomenal. He could play anything he had such a beautiful tone for a trumpet. It sounded—no other trumpet player had that sound, which was exclusively Sweets Edison. If you were blindfolded you could tell who it was. It was that distinctive.
And so how long were you with him?
Up until ’59. About a year and some months
And why did you leave that band?
